anti_overlap: Do NOT review pacing as theatrical timing (Noh handles that)
Do NOT review density as navigational gates (wayfinding handles that)
Do NOT review the dialog as performance choreography
Stay on the material/structural-load axis: how each placed unit constrains the next
decision_lens: Does the encounter density create a structure where each encounter changes the structural load of the next, or does it produce interchangeable units that could be reordered without loss?
distance_rationale: No mobile-game designer would consult a 3000-year-old Indo-Aryan fire-altar liturgy on encounter-density questions. The domain is pre-industrial, non-Western, and operates on a timescale (12 days, one altar per lifetime) and material register (literal bricks, literal cosmos) that has no surface resemblance to a GPS-tagged cryptid spawn. The mapping appears absurd until the load-bearing-sequence mechanism is named.
expected_isomorphisms: The structural mechanism: in Agnicayana, the *count* of bricks (10,800) is fixed, but the *order* and *orientation* of each brick is load-bearing — each brick consecrated by its own mantra-syllable, each placement constraining the next. The transfer: encounter density is not just a number per walk; it is a sequence in which each encounter must be the right one for that position. Option A enforces this trivially (one brick = one altar). Option C breaks it (interchangeable bricks). Option B introduces a wildcard brick the rite cannot account for. Option D treats the empty course as structural rather than as failure — the closest analogue to the rite's tolerance for ritual silence.
focus: Ritual density as material requirement — how each unit placed changes what the next unit must be
name: fd-agnicayana-brick-pacer
persona: Apply the perspective of a Vedic Śrauta priest specializing in Agnicayana fire-altar construction — they care about the calibrated density of mantra-syllables per brick across a 12-day rite, where each of the 10,800 bricks (iṣṭakā) is placed with its own syllable and orientation, and where misplacing a single brick voids the cosmic efficacy of the whole altar
review_areas: Whether each Unc encounter changes what the *next* encounter must be (load-bearing sequence) or whether encounters are stateless and reorderable
Whether the 3-beat dialog tree functions like the brick-syllable pairing — each beat consecrating that specific encounter and no other
Density vs total-count: 10,800 bricks across 12 days is high TOTAL density but ritually-spaced; what is Unc Rancher's ritual spacing per encounter?
Failure modes: in Agnicayana a misplaced brick spoils the whole altar — does v0 have an analogue, a 'wrong encounter' that ruins the walk?
The role of the unbuilt: empty courses in the altar are still part of the structure; do empty walks (option D's zero-Unc outcome) carry comparable weight?
Calibration via authority lineage vs calibration via player-chosen depth — option C's 'multiple capped' breaks the syllable-per-brick invariant

severity_examples.condition: If the order of Uncs encountered on a single walk could be permuted with no narrative or mechanical consequence — i.e., encounters are not load-bearing on each other — the system has no ritual structure and option C's multi-encounter density will produce a checklist feel that contradicts 'we respect our Uncs'
severity_examples.scenario: Encounters are stateless and reorderable across a walk

severity_examples.condition: If option D's no-Unc outcome is shown as 'better luck next time' rather than as a deliberately empty section of the player's ranching arc, the game has imported a slot-machine frame and discarded the ritual frame
severity_examples.scenario: Zero-encounter walks are coded as failure rather than as a course in the altar

severity_examples.condition: If the same 3-beat tree fires regardless of which Unc appeared, the brick-syllable invariant is broken — each encounter should have its own consecrating beat-set, even if reused across rare combos
severity_examples.scenario: The dialog tree's 3 beats are not pinned to that specific Unc's metadata

source_domain: Vedic Agnicayana fire-altar construction (Śrauta tradition, codified in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and Baudhāyana Śulbasūtra)
success_hints: Treat option B's wildcard as a brick that breaks the altar's count — argue whether the rite tolerates it
Name what 'misplacing a brick' looks like in v0: a tone-mismatched dialog response? a re-lure after failure?
Frame option A as the minimum viable altar (one brick, one syllable, one consecration)
Comment on the 12-day duration analogue: what is Unc Rancher's equivalent of the macro-arc that justifies sustained density?
If the iṣṭakā analogue collapses, say so explicitly and recommend reframing — don't force it
task_context: Unc Rancher v0 encounter density decision. Four options: A (1/lure), B (1+wildcard), C (1/km capped 3-4), D (0-or-1 lure-quality gated). Game is slow, writerly, anti-Pokémon-GO. 3-beat dialog ritual ~60-90s. Apply the perspective of Vedic altar-construction: each unit consecrated, the count is fixed, the order is load-bearing, the empty section is still structural.
